name: PySeq
role: Python library and CLI that lists numbered frame files as ranges with missing frames
summary: Python library and CLI suite (`lss`, `stree`, `sfind`, `sdiff`, `sstat`, `scopy`, `smv`, `srm`) that groups numbered files such as `frame.0001.png` into sequences and reports ranges like `[1-3, 6-7, 10]` and the exact missing frames. It reads file names only, never pixels.
use_when: Check a capture or render folder has every frame before encoding, with the missing numbers listed
List which sequences sit in a folder, with start, end and length
avoid_when: Encoding or reading pixels from a sequence: FFmpeg or OpenImageIO
A one-off check of a single known range: a shell loop is enough

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install pyseq==0.9.3

notes: 2026-11-27: lead said `uv tool install`; the fixture uses a pinned pip venv instead. Lead version 0.9.3 and BSD-3-Clause confirmed on PyPI.

2026-11-27: non-frame files such as notes.txt are returned as one-item sequences, and mixed padding (001, 002, 0100) merges into one sequence with false missing frames; filter and normalise before use.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 0.9.3 (2026-07-25), BSD-3-Clause, no dependencies, repository pushed 2026-08-24. ffmpeg-ffprobe and openimageio-oiiotool read sequences but do not report which frames are missing. Overlaps a shell loop for a known range, so keep as a candidate, not core.

evidence.result: 5 of 7 checks pass, repeat processes identical: gap [1-3, 6-7, 10] gives missing 4,5,8,9; 1001-1005 gives missing 1003; lss prints the range line. KNOWN FAIL: notes.txt listed as a sequence; pad.001/002 + pad.0100 merge with 97 false missing frames.
evidence.scope: Empty generated files, names only, Python 3.12 macOS arm64: gaps and ranges correct; stray files and mixed padding not handled; no pixels, duplicates or other CLIs.
